title: The dog and the envelope
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The envelope, unopened, day two. The dog sniffs it, considers it, and lies down on it. Wood lets him. It's warmer there. Nobody says the word Portland.

panels.composition: The envelope on the desk. BARNABY's nose at it.

image.prompt: close on a small dog's nose sniffing a thick envelope on a desk, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The dog climbing onto the desk — allowed today — and lying on the envelope. WOOD moving the pad to make room.

image.prompt: a small dog lying down on top of an envelope on a desk while a young man shifts his drawing pad aside, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The envelope's corner under the dog's chin. PORTLAND, half covered.

image.prompt: close on the corner of an envelope with a printed word half hidden under a sleeping dog's chin, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood drawing around the dog. The strip, the dog, the envelope, the desk. Nobody says the word.

image.prompt: a young man drawing at a desk crowded by a small dog asleep on an envelope, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: Day two. The dog lies on it. The word is not said.
